scenario: 面试题「给 LinkedIn/Facebook 设计 feed 排序」，它和纯视频/内容推荐共享排序原理，但多了几个独有维度。
scenario_en: The prompt 'design feed ranking for LinkedIn/Facebook' shares ranking principles with pure content rec but adds several unique dimensions.
q: 社交 feed 排序相比纯内容推荐，独有的三个新维度是什么？
q_en: What three dimensions does social feed ranking add beyond pure content recommendation?
why: 社交 feed 多了：社交图谱(纯内容推荐没有的关系信号)、以小时计的新鲜度(不是天)、异构内容(文本/图片/转发/投票/插播广告)争夺同一个视口。这三点决定了它的数据、延迟和建模都不同。
why_en: Social feed adds a social graph (relationship signals absent in content rec), freshness in hours not days, and heterogeneous content (text/images/reshares/polls/ads) competing for one viewport.
diagram:
flowchart TB F["社交 feed 排序"] --> G["社交图谱
关系信号"] F --> H["小时级新鲜度
near-real-time"] F --> C["异构内容
争一个视口"]
options: 更大规模的排序模型、更多 GPU 算力、更长的离线训练周期
更高的视频分辨率、更优的转码质量、更快的 CDN 边缘分发
社交图谱关系信号、小时级新鲜度、异构内容争夺同一视口
更多的广告位库存、更高的实时出价、更精细的定向策略
options_en: A larger ranking model, more GPU compute, and longer offline training cycles.
Higher video resolution, better transcoding quality, and faster CDN edge delivery.
Social-graph relationship signals, hour-scale freshness, heterogeneous content competing for one viewport.
More ad-slot inventory, higher real-time bids, and finer-grained targeting.
optionExplanations: 模型规模/算力/训练周期是通用 ML 工程量，不是社交 feed 相对内容推荐的独有维度。
分辨率/转码/CDN 分发是视频内容分发问题，与社交 feed 的关系信号无关。
对；关系图谱、小时级新鲜、异构内容争视口正是社交 feed 的三个独有维度。
广告位/出价/定向是可显式划为范围外的广告排序子问题，不是 feed 排序本身的独有新维度。
optionExplanations_en: Model scale/compute/training cycles are generic ML engineering, not a dimension unique to social feed vs content rec.
Resolution/transcoding/CDN delivery is a video-distribution concern, unrelated to social feed's relationship signals.
Correct — the relationship graph, hour-scale freshness, and heterogeneous content competing for one viewport are social feed's three unique dimensions.
Ad slots/bids/targeting are an ad-ranking sub-problem you can explicitly scope out, not a unique dimension of feed ranking itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录用户之间关注/好友/互动关系的图，是 feed 排序独有的高信息量信号源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A social graph records follow/friend/interaction relationships between users, a high-signal source unique to feed ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户屏幕上一次能看到的内容区域，各种异构内容都要争这块位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The viewport is the content area visible on screen at once, which all heterogeneous content competes to occupy.

scenario: 面试开场要先讲清 feed 排序在优化哪些业务目标。
scenario_en: Opening the interview, you must state which business objectives feed ranking optimizes.
q: 社交 feed 排序的三个核心业务指标是哪些？(多选)
q_en: What are the three core business metrics of social feed ranking? (multiple)
why: 三大业务指标是参与度、有意义连接、创作者公平——它们互相拉扯，应先全摆出来再问面试官优先哪个，这是产品成熟度的信号。
why_en: The three are engagement, meaningful connections, and creator equity; they pull against each other, so state all three then ask which to prioritize.
options: 参与度(engagement)：会话时长、点击、评论、转发
有意义的连接(meaningful connections)：回复、私信、熟人间评论串
创作者公平(creator equity)：跨粉丝层级的公平曝光份额
CDN 缓存命中率：静态资源分发效率
options_en: Engagement: session time, clicks, comments, reshares.
Meaningful connections: replies, DMs, comment threads between mutuals.
Creator equity: fair impression share across follower tiers.
CDN cache hit rate: static-asset delivery efficiency.
optionExplanations: 对；参与度最可测，是默认优化目标，但过头会放大标题党。
对；有意义连接关联长期留存，是 FB 2018 年重心转移的目标。
对；创作者公平保证内容供给侧不至于赢家通吃，是双边市场的一极。
错；这是纯运维指标，跟参与度/连接/公平这三个业务目标不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — engagement is most measurable and the default target, but over-doing it amplifies clickbait.
Correct — meaningful connections correlate with long-term retention, the target of Facebook's 2018 pivot.
Correct — creator equity keeps the supply side from winner-take-all, one pole of the two-sided market.
Wrong — that is a pure ops metric, not one of the three business objectives (engagement/connections/equity).

termDefinitions.meaning: 让不同粉丝量级的创作者获得公平曝光份额，避免赢家通吃、供给枯竭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Creator equity gives creators of different follower tiers a fair impression share, avoiding winner-take-all and supply starvation.

scenario: 参与度是最可测、最常被当默认优化目标的业务指标。
scenario_en: Engagement is the most measurable business metric and the default optimization target.
q: 参与度常用什么 ML 代理目标，主要风险是什么？
q_en: What ML proxy objective does engagement use, and what is its main risk?
why: 参与度用 P(click) 或 E[dwell time](停留时长)当代理，它最可测、直接关联广告收入和黏性。但纯追它会放大标题党，把煽动/浅层内容顶上来，侵蚀更深层的连接。
why_en: Engagement proxies as P(click) or E[dwell time]—most measurable, tied to ad revenue and stickiness—but chasing it amplifies clickbait, surfacing sensational shallow content.
options: 代理目标是 P(click)/E[dwell time]，风险是放大标题党/煽动内容
代理目标是曝光公平约束，风险是短期参与度下降
代理目标是 P(meaningful interaction)，风险是标签稀疏难测
代理目标是 CDN 命中率，风险是缓存失效
options_en: Proxy is P(click)/E[dwell time]; the risk is amplifying clickbait/sensational content.
Proxy is an exposure-fairness constraint; the risk is lower short-term engagement.
Proxy is P(meaningful interaction); the risk is sparse, hard-to-measure labels.
Proxy is CDN hit rate; the risk is cache invalidation.
optionExplanations: 对；参与度最可测，代理是 P(click)/E[dwell]，代价是易被标题党套利。
曝光公平约束是创作者公平的代理，不是参与度的。
P(meaningful interaction) 是有意义连接的代理，标签稀疏是它的风险，非参与度。
CDN 命中率是基础设施指标，不是参与度的 ML 代理。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — engagement is most measurable, proxied by P(click)/E[dwell], at the cost of clickbait arbitrage.
An exposure-fairness constraint is the proxy for creator equity, not engagement.
P(meaningful interaction) is the meaningful-connections proxy, with sparse labels as its risk, not engagement's.
CDN hit rate is an infrastructure metric, not an ML proxy for engagement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户在一条内容上停留的时间，是参与度的常用代理信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dwell time is how long a user lingers on a piece of content, a common engagement proxy.

scenario: 参与度和有意义的连接是两个不同的业务目标，可测性和风险都不一样。
scenario_en: Engagement and meaningful connections are two different objectives with different measurability and risks.
q: 参与度和「有意义的连接」在可测性与风险上如何对比？
q_en: How do engagement and meaningful connections contrast on measurability and risk?
why: 参与度最可测(点击/停留)、风险是标题党；有意义连接(回复/私信/评论串)关联长期留存但标签稀疏、难测。前者好优化易走偏，后者难测却更保长期，两者常反向拉扯。
why_en: Engagement is highly measurable (clicks/dwell) but risks clickbait; meaningful connections (replies/DMs/threads) correlate with long-term retention but have sparse, hard-to-measure labels, and they pull against each other.
tradeoff: 参与度(好测·易被标题党套利) vs 有意义连接(难测·更护长期留存)
options: 两者的可测性和风险其实完全一样，只是换了个说法而已
说反了：其实有意义连接才最好测，参与度反而是难测的那个
参与度其实是靠曝光公平约束来衡量的，有意义连接反而靠点击衡量
参与度好测但易被标题党套利；有意义连接难测但更护长期留存
options_en: Both are equally measurable with identical risk, just described using different names.
It's backwards: meaningful connections are actually the most measurable, and engagement is the hard one.
Engagement is actually measured by an exposure-fairness constraint, while meaningful connections are measured by clicks.
Engagement is measurable but clickbait-prone; meaningful connections are hard to measure but protect long-term retention.
optionExplanations: 两者可测性和风险明显不同，不是同物换名。
说反了：参与度最好测，有意义连接标签稀疏最难测。
代理搞混了：曝光公平是创作者公平的代理，点击是参与度的代理。
对；这条对比正是产品要权衡的核心——好测的易走偏，难测的更护长期。
optionExplanations_en: Their measurability and risk clearly differ; not the same thing renamed.
Backwards: engagement is most measurable while meaningful connections have sparse labels and are hardest to measure.
Proxies mixed up: exposure fairness proxies creator equity, and clicks proxy engagement.
Correct — this contrast is the core product trade-off: the measurable one drifts, the hard one protects the long term.

termDefinitions.term: meaningful connections / 有意义的连接
termDefinitions.meaning: 由内容触发的回复、私信、熟人间评论串，关联长期留存但标签稀疏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Meaningful connections are content-triggered replies, DMs, and threads between mutuals, tied to long-term retention but sparsely labeled.

scenario: Facebook 2018 年做过一次著名的排序重心调整。
scenario_en: Facebook made a famous ranking re-weighting in 2018.
q: Facebook 2018 年的「meaningful social interactions」调整改了什么？
q_en: What did Facebook's 2018 'meaningful social interactions' shift change?
why: 它把排序权重从「原始参与度」重新分配到「有意义的社交互动」——更看重评论串深度、熟人回复，而非被动点赞/浏览。目的是保长期留存，代价是可能压低短期参与量。
why_en: It re-weighted ranking from raw engagement toward meaningful social interactions—favoring comment-thread depth and replies between mutuals over passive likes—to protect long-term retention.
options: 把整个排序逻辑完全交给广告竞价系统，价高者直接置顶
从原始参与度重新加权到有意义社交互动，护长期留存
取消所有个性化，改成纯粹按时间倒序排列的 feed
只保留视频内容，把文本和图片帖全部下线
options_en: Handed the entire ranking logic to an ad-auction system, pinning the highest bidder.
Re-weighted from raw engagement toward meaningful social interactions, protecting long-term retention.
Removed all personalization and switched to a purely reverse-chronological feed.
Kept only video content and retired all text and image posts.
optionExplanations: MSI 调整是重排业务目标，不是把 feed 交给广告出价。
对；核心是把权重从被动参与移到有意义互动，赌的是长期留存而非短期量。
MSI 不是取消个性化，反而是更精细地重排目标权重。
MSI 与内容类型下线无关，改的是目标权重不是内容池。
optionExplanations_en: The MSI shift re-weighted business objectives, not handed the feed to ad bids.
Correct — the core was moving weight from passive engagement to meaningful interaction, betting on long-term retention over short-term volume.
MSI did not remove personalization; it re-weighted objectives more finely.
MSI has nothing to do with retiring content types; it changed objective weights, not the content pool.

termDefinitions.meaning: Facebook 2018 排序重心：更看重评论串深度与熟人回复，而非被动点赞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MSI (Meaningful Social Interactions) is Facebook's 2018 ranking focus favoring thread depth and replies between mutuals over passive likes.

scenario: 如果只按参与度排序、完全不管创作者曝光是否公平。
scenario_en: If you rank purely by engagement and ignore whether creator exposure is fair.
q: 缺少创作者公平会让 feed 生态出什么问题？
q_en: What happens to the feed ecosystem without creator equity?
why: 没有公平约束，曝光会向头部集中形成赢家通吃：小创作者拿不到曝光→内容供给侧枯竭→多样性下降。创作者是双边市场的供给侧，饿死供给会反噬整个平台。
why_en: Without a fairness constraint, exposure concentrates into winner-take-all: small creators starve of impressions, the supply side dries up, and diversity degrades.
options: 曝光向头部集中、赢家通吃，小创作者供给枯竭、多样性下降
所有创作者的曝光会自动变得均等，完全不需要任何人为干预
只会影响广告收入，跟内容供给侧完全没有关系
短期和长期指标会同时一起上升，完全没有任何代价
options_en: Exposure concentrates into winner-take-all, starving small creators and degrading supply and diversity.
All creators' exposure automatically becomes equal, with no human intervention needed at all.
It would only affect ad revenue, with no relationship to the content supply side at all.
Short- and long-term metrics would rise together all at once, with no cost whatsoever.
optionExplanations: 对；纯参与度排序自我强化头部，饿死供给侧，是双边市场的核心风险。
自动均等是幻想：参与度排序天然向头部集中，不干预只会更不均。
供给侧枯竭直接减少可推内容和多样性，不只是广告问题。
赢家通吃短期或许好看，长期供给枯竭会反噬，绝非没有代价。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — pure engagement ranking self-reinforces the top and starves the supply side, the core two-sided-market risk.
Automatic equality is fantasy: engagement ranking naturally concentrates at the top, and no intervention worsens it.
Supply starvation directly reduces recommendable content and diversity, not just ad revenue.
Winner-take-all may look fine short-term, but long-term supply starvation bites back—hardly costless.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时服务消费者(看)和创作者(供给)的平台，供给侧枯竭会拖垮整体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-sided market serves both consumers (viewers) and creators (supply); starving the supply side drags the whole platform down.

scenario: 面试开场,你识别出参与度、有意义连接、创作者公平三个目标彼此拉扯,但不知道该主推哪个。
scenario_en: Opening the interview, you spot that engagement, meaningful connections, and creator equity pull against each other but don't know which to prioritize.
q: 面对三个互相冲突的目标,开场该怎么处理?
q_en: Facing three conflicting objectives, how should you handle the opening?
why: 先把三个目标都点出来、说清它们互相拉扯,再显式问面试官优先哪个——真实系统就是要做刻意的取舍。默认闷头只优化参与度会显得没有产品思维。
why_en: State all three objectives and their tension explicitly, then ask the interviewer which to prioritize, because real systems make deliberate trade-offs.
tradeoff: 先陈述三目标再问优先级(显产品成熟) vs 默认只优化参与度(缺取舍视角)
options: 直接默认优先优化参与度,因为它数据最全、最容易衡量,完全不必再多问
自己在心里随便挑一个目标就闷头设计架构,等做完了才跟面试官说选的是哪个
彻底回避三个目标间的冲突,只谈存储和排序架构细节、绝口不提任何业务权衡
把三个目标都陈述清楚、点明它们互相拉扯,再问面试官优先哪个
options_en: Default straight to prioritizing engagement since it has the most data and is easiest to measure, no need to ask at all.
Silently pick one objective and design the architecture heads-down, only telling the interviewer which one once it's done.
Thoroughly avoid the tension among the three objectives and discuss only storage/ranking architecture details, never the business trade-offs.
State all three objectives, point out their tension, then ask the interviewer which to prioritize.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官已在题面明确指定主目标(如「就最大化参与度」),则不必再问,直接据此展开设计更高效。
optionExplanations: 默认参与度会错过面试官想考的取舍,也暴露缺产品视角。
随便挑一个不沟通,可能整道题都朝错误优先级做,返工代价大。
回避业务权衡恰恰丢掉了这道题最核心的考点。
对;陈述三目标+主动问优先级,是展示产品成熟度的标准开场。
optionExplanations_en: Defaulting to engagement misses the trade-off the interviewer wants and shows a lack of product view.
Picking one without communicating risks building the whole answer on the wrong priority, costing a rework later.
Avoiding the business trade-off drops the very thing this question tests.
Correct — stating the three and asking the priority is the standard opening that signals product maturity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在多个互相冲突的业务目标里,和干系人确认先优化哪个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Objective prioritization is confirming with stakeholders which of several conflicting business goals to optimize first.

scenario: 监控发现:每日参与度持续上升,但 30 天留存却在下降。
scenario_en: Monitoring shows daily engagement rising while 30-day retention declines.
q: 「日参与涨、30 天留存跌」最可能说明什么?
q_en: What does 'daily engagement up but 30-day retention down' most likely indicate?
why: 这是在以有意义互动为代价换取浅层参与:排序顶起了能骗即时点击/停留但让人后悔的内容,短期数字好看、长期用户慢慢流失。信号就是短期参与与长期留存背离。
why_en: It signals optimizing for shallow engagement at the expense of meaningful interactions—content that farms immediate clicks but erodes long-term retention.
options: 这是模型欠拟合导致排序不准的表现,应该加大模型规模继续堆参与度指标
在以有意义互动为代价换取浅层参与,短期数字好但长期留存被侵蚀
这纯属短期随机噪声波动,不必理会,过阵子留存数字自己会慢慢恢复正常
说明创作者公平约束设置得太强,压低了整体参与度但对留存本身没有影响
options_en: It shows the model underfitting and ranking inaccurately; scale up the model and keep piling on engagement.
It trades meaningful interaction for shallow engagement—good short-term numbers but eroding long-term retention.
This is purely short-term random noise; ignore it, and the retention number will slowly recover on its own.
It means the creator-equity constraint is set too strong, suppressing overall engagement but not affecting retention itself.
optionExplanations: 加大模型继续堆参与度只会加剧浅层化,方向反了。
对;短期参与与长期留存背离,是浅层参与蚕食有意义互动的典型信号。
30 天留存持续下降不是噪声,是系统性趋势,必须响应。
留存下降的锅在浅层参与,不是创作者公平;后者一般压的是短期参与不是留存。
optionExplanations_en: Scaling up to pile on engagement worsens shallowness—the wrong direction.
Correct — short-term engagement diverging from long-term retention is the classic sign of shallow engagement cannibalizing meaningful interaction.
A sustained 30-day retention decline is not noise but a systematic trend that must be addressed.
The retention drop is on shallow engagement, not creator equity, which typically suppresses short-term engagement rather than retention.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户在 30 天窗口内是否仍活跃,是长期健康的核心指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 30-day retention is whether users remain active within a 30-day window, a core long-term health metric.

scenario: 约 20 亿日活,每次刷新要从好友/群组/主页/广告里汇聚几百到几千条候选帖。
scenario_en: About 2B DAU; each refresh must assemble hundreds to thousands of candidate posts from friends/groups/pages/ads.
q: feed 排序里的「fan-out 问题」指的是什么?
q_en: What is the 'fan-out problem' in feed ranking?
why: fan-out 问题是:一条帖子要分发到大量关注者的 feed、或一次刷新要从大量来源汇聚候选,在 20 亿日活规模下,分发/汇聚的存储与计算成本爆炸,必须选 fan-out on write / read / 混合策略。
why_en: The fan-out problem is distributing a post to many followers' feeds (or assembling candidates from many sources) at 2B-DAU scale, where the write/read cost explodes and forces a fan-out-on-write/read/hybrid choice.
diagram:
flowchart LR P["一条新帖"] --> W{"如何送达
关注者 feed?"} W -->|写时分发| A["预推进每个粉丝 feed"] W -->|读时汇聚| B["请求时拉取合并"]
options: 训练时模型权重 fan-out 太多导致过拟合,需要加正则化的问题
一条帖要分发到大量关注者、或一次刷新要汇聚大量来源,规模下存储/计算成本爆炸
GPU 显存容量不足导致训练 batch 无法正常 fan-out 的硬件资源问题
CDN 边缘节点缓存容量不够、无法 fan-out 静态资源的分发问题
options_en: A training-time problem where model weights fan out too much and overfit, requiring more regularization.
Distributing one post to many followers (or assembling many sources per refresh), where storage/compute cost explodes at scale.
A hardware problem where GPU memory capacity is too small to fan out the training batch normally.
A delivery problem where CDN edge nodes lack cache capacity to fan out static assets.
optionExplanations: fan-out 不是模型正则概念,而是 feed 分发/汇聚的系统扩展问题。
对;核心是海量关注者/来源下的分发与汇聚成本,决定写扩散还是读扩散。
不是 GPU 显存问题,是 feed 存储/计算的扩展权衡。
不是 CDN 静态分发,而是社交关系图上的 feed 分发。
optionExplanations_en: Fan-out is not a model-regularization concept but a systems-scaling problem of feed distribution/assembly.
Correct — the core is distribution and assembly cost under massive followers/sources, deciding write vs read fan-out.
Not a GPU memory issue but a feed storage/compute scaling trade-off.
Not CDN static delivery but feed distribution over the social graph.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一条帖子分发到众多关注者 feed(写扩散)或请求时从众多来源汇聚(读扩散)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is distributing a post to many followers' feeds (on write) or assembling from many sources at request time (on read).

termDefinitions.meaning: 日活跃用户数,这里约 20 亿,是估算分发/汇聚规模的基数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU (Daily Active Users), here ~2 billion, is the base for sizing distribution/assembly scale.

scenario: 普通用户粉丝不多、写帖不频繁,但读 feed 要极低延迟。
scenario_en: An ordinary user has few followers and posts infrequently, but reading the feed needs very low latency.
q: 对普通用户,fan-out on write 为什么合适,代价是什么?
q_en: For ordinary users, why does fan-out on write fit, and at what cost?
why: 写扩散在发帖时就把帖子预推进每个关注者的 feed 存储,读 feed 时直接取、延迟极低。代价是存储放大+写放大;粉丝越多写扩散越贵,到百万粉就是「名人问题」。普通用户粉丝少,写扩散划算。
why_en: Fan-out on write pre-pushes a post into every follower's feed store at creation, so reads are ultra-low-latency; the cost is storage and write amplification, which explodes for millions of followers (the celebrity problem), so it fits low-follower ordinary users.
tradeoff: 写扩散(读快·但写/存放大) vs 读扩散(省写·但读时现算慢)
options: 发帖时预推进关注者 feed,读快;代价是存储写放大,粉丝越多越贵
请求时才现场从各个来源拉取全部数据现算,代价是读延迟明显变得很高
完全不做任何预计算,只靠一层缓存兜底,代价是容易出现缓存穿透问题
把帖子只存在作者本地节点上,代价是所有关注者都读不到这条帖
options_en: Pre-push into each follower's feed at post time, fast reads; the cost is storage/write amplification that grows with follower count.
Assemble and rank on the fly at request time by pulling from every source live; the cost is noticeably higher read latency.
Do no precomputation at all and rely purely on one cache layer; the cost is a higher chance of cache-penetration issues.
Store the post only on the author's local node; the cost is that every follower ends up completely unable to read it.
whenOtherWins: 当账号粉丝到百万级(名人),写扩散的存储/写放大变得不可承受,该改用 fan-out on read 请求时汇聚。
optionExplanations: 对;写扩散把成本前置到写路径换极快读,普通用户粉丝少写放大可控,划算。
请求时现拉是 fan-out on read 的特征,不是写扩散。
不预计算靠缓存不是写扩散的定义;写扩散恰恰是主动预推。
只存作者本地根本没做扩散,关注者读不到帖,不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — fan-out on write front-loads cost to the write path for very fast reads; ordinary users' low follower count keeps write amplification manageable.
On-the-fly assembly is fan-out on read's trait, not write.
Relying on cache without precompute is not the write-fan-out definition; write fan-out actively pre-pushes.
Storing only on the author's node does no fan-out at all, so followers cannot read—invalid.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发帖时就把内容推进每个关注者的 feed 存储,读时直接取,读快但写/存放大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on write pushes a post into every follower's feed store at creation, making reads fast but amplifying writes/storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次写操作触发大量下游写(推进百万粉丝 feed),放大写成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification is one write triggering many downstream writes (into millions of feeds), inflating write cost.

scenario: 某名人账号有上千万粉丝,一条帖若写扩散要推进上千万个 feed。
scenario_en: A celebrity account has tens of millions of followers; a single post would push into tens of millions of feeds under write fan-out.
q: 对超高粉丝账号,为什么 fan-out on read 更合适,代价是什么?
q_en: For very high-follower accounts, why does fan-out on read fit better, and at what cost?
why: 读扩散不预推,请求时才把该名人的帖拉进候选池合并,避免了写扩散推进千万 feed 的爆炸写放大。代价是读路径要在紧预算内实时汇聚+排序,对低延迟推理要求高。
why_en: Fan-out on read does not pre-push; it pulls the celebrity's posts into the candidate pool at request time, avoiding the explosive write amplification, at the cost of needing low-latency assembly and ranking on the read path.
tradeoff: 读扩散(避免名人写爆炸·但读时现算) vs 写扩散(读快·但名人写放大爆炸)
options: 预先把帖子推进上千万个粉丝各自的 feed 存储里,代价只是读的时候会变得很快
直接把名人发的帖子全部删掉不推送,代价是粉丝完全看不到任何内容
只给名人单独建一个独立的数据库分区,代价是这样反而无法参与排序
请求时才把名人帖拉进候选池合并,避免写爆炸;代价是读路径要低延迟实时汇聚
options_en: Pre-push each post into tens of millions of follower feed stores ahead of time; the only cost is that reads become fast.
Directly delete all of the celebrity's posts and never push them; the cost is followers can't see any content at all.
Give the celebrity their own separate database partition; the cost is that this actually keeps them out of ranking.
Pull the celebrity's posts into the candidate pool at request time, avoiding the write explosion; the cost is low-latency real-time assembly.
whenOtherWins: 对粉丝很少的普通账号,读扩散每次现拉反而浪费,写扩散预推、读时直接取更省更快。
optionExplanations: 预推千万 feed 正是要避免的写爆炸,是写扩散不是读扩散。
删帖不推是放弃分发,不是读扩散策略。
独立库不解决扩散问题,也不是「无法排序」;偷换概念。
对;读扩散把名人帖延后到请求时汇聚,避开写放大,代价是读路径实时算的延迟压力。
optionExplanations_en: Pre-pushing millions of feeds is exactly the write explosion to avoid—that's write fan-out, not read.
Deleting posts is abandoning distribution, not a read-fan-out strategy.
A separate DB does not solve fan-out and does not make ranking impossible; a bait-and-switch.
Correct — read fan-out defers celebrity posts to request-time assembly, dodging write amplification at the cost of real-time read-path latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不预推,请求时才把关注对象的帖拉进候选池合并排序,省写但读时现算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on read skips pre-pushing and assembles a follower's posts into the candidate pool at request time, saving writes but computing on reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 超高粉丝账号发帖若写扩散,要推进千万级 feed,写放大不可承受。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The celebrity problem is that a very-high-follower account's post under write fan-out must push into millions of feeds, an unbearable write amplification.

scenario: 既有海量普通用户(粉丝少),也有少数百万粉名人,单一 fan-out 策略两头不讨好。
scenario_en: There are many ordinary users (few followers) and a few million-follower celebrities; a single fan-out strategy serves neither well.
q: 生产系统怎么用混合 fan-out 兼顾两类账号?
q_en: How does production use hybrid fan-out to serve both account types?
why: 混合:普通用户走写扩散(读快、写放大可控);高粉丝名人走读扩散(避免写爆炸),请求时拉进候选池合并。中间放一层 feed cache 缓存已排好的结果,减少重复排序调用。
why_en: Hybrid: ordinary users fan out on write (fast reads, manageable amplification); high-follower accounts fan out on read (avoid the write explosion), merged into the candidate pool at request time, with a feed cache in between to cut redundant ranking.
tradeoff: 混合(按账号类型分策略·最优但更复杂) vs 单一策略(简单但对另一类账号失灵)
options: 所有账号无论类型统统走写扩散,连千万粉丝的名人账号也要预推进 feed 存储
所有账号无论类型统统走读扩散,连粉丝很少的普通用户也得请求时才现算
普通用户走写扩散、名人走读扩散,请求时合并,加 cache 减少重复排序
随机给每个账号分配写扩散或读扩散,单纯只是想借此均摊系统负载而已
options_en: Fan out on write for every account regardless of type, pre-pushing even million-follower celebrities into feed storage.
Fan out on read for every account regardless of type, forcing even low-follower ordinary users to compute on the fly.
Write fan-out for ordinary users, read fan-out for celebrities, merged at request time, with a cache layer cutting redundant ranking.
Randomly assign write fan-out or read fan-out to each account, purely hoping to spread the system load that way.
whenOtherWins: 若平台没有名人级账号(粉丝分布均匀且都不大),纯写扩散更简单,不必上混合的复杂度。
optionExplanations: 全写扩散在名人处触发写爆炸,正是混合要规避的。
全读扩散让普通用户每次读都现算,浪费本可预推的低延迟。
对;按账号类型分策略是生产标准解,feed cache 再砍掉重复排序开销。
随机分配无视账号粉丝规模,既不省名人写也不快普通读,没有依据。
optionExplanations_en: All-write triggers the write explosion at celebrities, exactly what hybrid avoids.
All-read makes ordinary users compute on every read, wasting the low latency a pre-push would give.
Correct — splitting strategy by account type is the production standard, and a feed cache further cuts redundant ranking.
Random assignment ignores follower scale, saving neither celebrity writes nor speeding ordinary reads—unfounded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 普通用户写扩散、高粉丝账号读扩散,请求时合并,兼顾读延迟与写成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hybrid fan-out uses write for ordinary users and read for high-follower accounts, merged at request time, balancing read latency and write cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 候选池与最终 feed 之间的缓存层,存已排好的结果,减少重复排序调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feed cache sits between the candidate pool and served feed, holding ranked results to cut redundant ranking calls.

scenario: feed 内容的半衰期以小时计,一条 12 小时前的帖子可能已经过时。
scenario_en: Feed content has a half-life in hours; a 12-hour-old post may already be stale.
q: 小时级新鲜度这个硬约束,对系统架构提出了什么要求?
q_en: What does the hour-scale freshness hard constraint demand of the architecture?
why: 新鲜度是硬约束:feed 是近实时系统不是批处理。模型要有时间衰减信号;服务要有近实时特征更新——最近的互动计数必须是当前的,不能是几小时前批处理跑出来的旧值。
why_en: Freshness is a hard constraint making feed a near-real-time system, not batch: the model needs time-decay signals and serving needs near-real-time feature updates so recent engagement counts are current, not hours-old batch values.
tradeoff: 近实时特征(新鲜准确·但流式基础设施重) vs 纯批处理(简单·但特征滞后数小时)
options: feed 是近实时系统:要时间衰减信号+近实时特征更新,互动计数不能是几小时前的旧值
feed 其实是纯批处理系统:每天只需要跑一次特征更新就够,新鲜度问题完全可以靠离线慢慢补齐
只要把缓存 TTL 调大一些,让旧内容在 feed 里多留一会儿即可彻底解决
新鲜度这件事只影响前端 UI 排版展示,完全不影响背后的模型和特征
options_en: Feed is near-real-time: it needs time-decay signals plus near-real-time feature updates, and engagement counts cannot be hours-old.
Feed is actually a purely batch system: a daily feature run is enough, and freshness can be fully patched offline over time.
Just turn up the cache TTL a bit, keeping old content around in the feed longer, and that fully solves it.
Freshness only affects front-end UI presentation, and has no effect on the model or features behind it at all.
whenOtherWins: 对更新极慢的特征(如社交图谱拓扑、用户长期画像),用每日批处理就够,不必上流式;只有快变的互动信号才需近实时。
optionExplanations: 对;小时级半衰期逼着整条链近实时,时间衰减+新鲜特征是硬要求。
批处理特征滞后数小时,会系统性错过正在爆发的内容,不满足新鲜度。
加大 TTL 是留住旧内容,恰恰和新鲜度背道而驰。
新鲜度直接决定模型特征时效,不只是 UI 排版。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — an hour-scale half-life forces the whole chain near-real-time; time-decay plus fresh features are hard requirements.
Batch features lag hours and systematically miss trending content, failing freshness.
Raising TTL keeps old content around, the opposite of freshness.
Freshness directly governs feature timeliness for the model, not just UI layout.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容的时效性,feed 半衰期以小时计,要求近实时特征与时间衰减信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Freshness is content timeliness; feed half-life is in hours, demanding near-real-time features and time-decay signals.

termDefinitions.term: time-decay signal / 时间衰减信号
termDefinitions.meaning: 让越新的内容得分越高、越旧越衰减的特征,兑现新鲜度约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A time-decay signal scores newer content higher and decays older content, honoring the freshness constraint.

scenario: 端到端 feed 延迟预算 <200ms,例:检索 ~50ms、排序 ~80ms、重排 ~40ms、feed cache TTL 失效 ~10ms。
scenario_en: End-to-end feed latency budget <200ms, e.g. retrieval ~50ms, ranking ~80ms, re-ranking ~40ms, feed cache TTL invalidation ~10ms.
q: <200ms 是什么性质的约束,超了会怎样?
q_en: What kind of constraint is <200ms, and what happens if you exceed it?
why: <200ms 是给定的产品目标(SLO),不是算出来的。它是检索+排序+重排各段之和的封顶,例值 50+80+40+10≈180ms;超预算会增加会话放弃(用户等不及就走)。所以每段延迟都要卡在预算内。
why_en: The <200ms is a given product SLO, not a computed value; it caps the sum of retrieval+ranking+re-ranking (e.g. 50+80+40+10≈180ms), and exceeding it raises session abandonment.
options: 它是衡量排序模型准确率高低的下限指标,跟端到端延迟预算完全无关
它是限制每日离线训练时长的一个上限,和线上实时服务完全无关
它是给定的产品 SLO,是各段延迟之和的封顶;超了会增加会话放弃
它是限制 feed 缓存最多能存多大的一个上限,一旦超过阈值就会直接触发 OOM
options_en: It measures a lower bound on the ranking model's accuracy, entirely unrelated to the end-to-end latency budget.
It is a ceiling limiting daily offline training time, entirely unrelated to online real-time serving.
It is a given product SLO capping the sum of stage latencies; exceeding it raises session abandonment.
It is a ceiling limiting how large the feed cache can grow; exceeding the threshold triggers an immediate OOM.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户因加载太慢而提前离开的比例,延迟超预算会推高它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Session abandonment is the share of users who leave early due to slow loading, which rises when latency exceeds budget.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对延迟等指标设定的目标阈值,这里是端到端 <200ms。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a target threshold for a metric like latency, here end-to-end <200ms.

optionExplanations: 错；这是模型质量指标，跟延迟预算不是一回事，200ms 管的是响应快慢。
错；训练时长是离线成本，不受制于在线请求的这条 200ms 时钟。
对；<200ms 是产品给定的 SLO，把检索+排序+重排各段加起来封顶，超了用户等不及就走。
错；缓存大小超限是内存问题，跟一次请求要多快返回没关系。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — that describes model quality, not the latency budget; the 200ms clock is about response speed.
Wrong — training time is an offline cost, not bound by this per-request 200ms clock.
Correct — <200ms is a given product SLO capping the sum of retrieval+ranking+re-ranking; blow it and users abandon the session.
Wrong — running out of cache space is a memory issue, unrelated to how fast one request must return.

scenario: Staff+ 面试想听你怎么框定整个 feed 系统的最高层视角。
scenario_en: A Staff+ interview wants to hear how you frame the whole feed system at the top level.
q: Staff+ 会把 feed 系统框成什么,并因此把什么当一等目标?
q_en: How does a Staff+ candidate frame the feed system, and what becomes a first-class objective?
why: 框成双边市场(消费者+创作者):不只优化看的人,还要维护创作者供给侧。因此创作者公平成为一等目标,配可度量的公平 SLO;还要考虑组织取舍(排序权重归 ML 还是产品团队)和二阶效应(参与农场)。
why_en: Frame it as a two-sided marketplace (consumers + creators), making creator equity a first-class objective with measurable fairness SLOs, plus org trade-offs and second-order effects.
tradeoff: 双边市场框架(护供给侧+公平 SLO) vs 单边消费者视角(只优化看的人·长期饿死供给)
options: 只框成一个纯消费者系统,一门心思只优化看的人的参与度指标
框成双边市场,创作者公平是一等目标,配可度量的公平 SLO
框成一个纯广告竞价的系统,谁出价最高谁就能拿到全部曝光
框成一个纯批处理的离线系统,彻底忽略掉所有实时性要求
options_en: Frame it purely as a consumer-only system, single-mindedly optimizing only viewers' engagement metric.
Frame it as a two-sided marketplace, with creator equity as a first-class objective and a measurable fairness SLO.
Frame it as a pure ad-auction system where the single highest bidder takes all the exposure.
Frame it as a purely batch offline system, completely ignoring every real-time requirement.
whenOtherWins: 若产品明确只做消费侧、内容全由自家 PGC 供给(没有第三方创作者生态),单边消费者框架就够,不必上双边市场。
optionExplanations: 只优化消费者会长期饿死创作者供给,缺了双边视角。
对;双边市场+创作者公平 SLO 是 Staff+ 的框架高度,兼顾供需两侧长期健康。
纯竞价忽略了内容质量和长期生态,不是 feed 排序的正确框架。
纯批处理违背 feed 的小时级新鲜度硬约束。
optionExplanations_en: Optimizing only consumers starves creator supply long-term, missing the two-sided view.
Correct — a two-sided marketplace plus creator-equity SLOs is the Staff+ framing altitude, balancing long-term health on both sides.
Pure auction ignores content quality and long-term ecosystem, not the right frame for feed ranking.
Pure batch violates feed's hour-scale freshness hard constraint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把创作者曝光公平设成可监控的目标阈值,越线告警,而非事后审计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fairness SLO makes creator exposure fairness a monitored target threshold with alerts, not a post-hoc audit.

scenario: 排序若奖励浅层互动,创作者会学着迎合算法而非做好内容。
scenario_en: If ranking rewards shallow interactions, creators learn to game the algorithm rather than make good content.
q: 「参与农场(engagement-farming)」是什么二阶效应?
q_en: What second-order effect is 'engagement-farming'?
why: 参与农场是创作者为迎合排序而刻意制造浅层互动(比如「评论区扣 1」「点赞抽奖」)来刷曝光,内容质量反而下降。这是激励结构被排序目标带偏的二阶效应,Staff+ 要能预见。
why_en: Engagement-farming is creators deliberately manufacturing shallow interactions (e.g. 'comment 1 below', like-giveaways) to game exposure, degrading content quality—a second-order effect of misaligned incentives that Staff+ should anticipate.
options: 创作者主动打磨内容质量、靠真实价值换取用户自然互动,是一种健康的正向效应
这是平台向第三方数据供应商批量购买真实用户互动的一种商业模式
这只是一种按互动量给创作者发放固定月薪的普通激励机制而已
创作者刻意制造浅层互动来刷曝光,内容质量下降,是激励被带偏的二阶效应
options_en: Creators actively polishing content quality to earn users' organic interaction through real value, a healthy positive effect.
A business model where the platform bulk-buys real user interactions from a third-party data vendor.
Just an ordinary incentive scheme that pays creators a fixed monthly salary based on interaction volume.
Creators manufacturing shallow interactions to game exposure, degrading quality—a second-order effect of misaligned incentives.
optionExplanations: 参与农场是刷浅层互动的负向套利,不是提升质量的正向效应。
不是买互动的商业模式,而是创作者为迎合算法的行为扭曲。
和发工资无关,是激励结构导致的内容退化。
对;它是排序目标错配诱发的创作者套利行为,预见它是 Staff+ 的系统思维。
optionExplanations_en: Engagement-farming is negative arbitrage of shallow interactions, not a positive quality lift.
Not a model of buying interactions but a behavioral distortion by creators gaming the algorithm.
Nothing to do with salaries; it is content degradation driven by the incentive structure.
Correct — it is creator arbitrage induced by a misaligned ranking objective, and anticipating it is Staff+ systems thinking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 创作者刻意制造浅层互动(评论区扣1、点赞抽奖)迎合排序刷曝光,内容质量下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Engagement-farming is creators manufacturing shallow interactions to game ranking for exposure, at the cost of content quality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统改动引发参与者行为改变后产生的间接后果,常被忽视。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A second-order effect is an indirect consequence arising after participants change behavior in response to a system change.

scenario: feed 排序题的前 5-8 分钟,要用一套开场把问题框清楚。
scenario_en: In the first 5-8 minutes of a feed-ranking question, frame the problem with a structured opener.
q: 把 feed 排序面试开场的 5 步排成推荐顺序:
q_en: Order the 5 steps of a feed-ranking interview opener:
steps: 澄清平台(LinkedIn 职场 / Facebook 社交 / Twitter 实时),内容与新鲜度不同
陈述业务目标(参与度/有意义连接/创作者公平),再问优先哪个
厘清规模数字(DAU、每日帖数、候选池大小、延迟预算)
点出 fan-out 取舍(普通写扩散、高粉读扩散,并解释为什么)
声明范围外(先排除广告排序、通知、搜索),防止范围蔓延
why: 开场顺序:先澄清平台(决定内容/新鲜度基调)→陈述业务目标并问优先级→厘清规模数字→点出 fan-out 取舍→声明范围外。这套顺序体现产品思维,也防止一上来就跳进架构细节。
why_en: Opener order: clarify the platform, state objectives and ask priority, scope the scale numbers, identify the fan-out trade-off, then declare out-of-scope—showing product thinking and avoiding jumping straight into architecture.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试中问题范围不断扩大导致答不完,靠开场声明范围外来控制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scope creep is the problem expanding until you can't finish; declaring out-of-scope up front controls it.

scenario: 把「为什么用混合 fan-out」讲成一条需求到缓解的完整链路。
scenario_en: Explain 'why hybrid fan-out' as one requirement-to-mitigation chain.
q: 把混合 fan-out 的决策链排成正确顺序(需求→性质→选择→代价→缓解):
q_en: Order the hybrid fan-out decision chain (requirement → property → choice → cost → mitigation):
steps: 需求:20 亿日活,读 feed 要低延迟,同时有百万粉名人
关键性质:普通用户适合预推,名人预推会写爆炸
选择:普通用户写扩散、名人读扩散,请求时合并候选池
代价:两条路径+读时现算增加系统复杂度和读延迟
缓解:中间加 feed cache 缓存已排结果,减少重复排序调用
why: 链路:先摆需求(低延迟读+名人存在)→点出关键性质(名人写扩散会爆炸)→选混合(普通写、名人读、合并)→承认代价(双路径+读延迟)→给缓解(feed cache 砍重复排序)。这条链能一口气讲清取舍。
why_en: The chain: state the requirement (low-latency reads plus celebrities), name the property (celebrity write fan-out explodes), choose hybrid (write for ordinary, read for celebrities, merged), admit the cost (dual paths + read latency), and mitigate with a feed cache.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  N["需求: 低延迟读+名人"] --> P["名人写扩散会爆炸"]
  P --> C["混合: 普通写/名人读/合并"]
  C --> K["代价: 双路径+读延迟"]
  K --> M["缓解: feed cache"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次请求要排序的帖子集合,由写扩散预推的和读扩散现拉的合并而成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The candidate pool is the set of posts to rank for one request, merged from write-fanned-out and read-fanned-out sources.

scenario: 同一道 feed 排序题,L4、L5、Staff+ 的作答范围不同。
scenario_en: For the same feed-ranking question, L4, L5, and Staff+ scope their answers differently.
q: L5 相比 L4,在作答范围上主要多了什么?
q_en: What does an L5 answer add in scope over an L4 answer?
why: L4 澄清主目标、内容类型、基本规模,定 1-2 个 ML 目标即可,不要求 fan-out 策略。L5 要多目标取舍、论证混合 fan-out、定离线+在线指标、识别数据源。
why_en: L4 clarifies the primary objective, content types, basic scale, defines 1-2 ML objectives and acknowledges latency; L5 adds multi-objective trade-offs, a justified hybrid fan-out, offline+online metrics, and data sources.
tradeoff: L5 多目标取舍+fan-out 策略+指标体系 vs L4 单目标+基本规模+认识延迟
options: 只是把同样深度的内容讲得更快一点、语速和口条更流利一点而已
多目标取舍、论证混合 fan-out、定离在线指标、找数据源
只是额外多画了一张看起来更复杂、连线更多的架构图而已
只是额外多背了几个听起来很厉害、但用不上的算法名词而已
options_en: Just delivering the same-depth content a bit faster, with a bit more fluent pacing and phrasing.
Multi-objective trade-offs, a justified hybrid fan-out, offline+online metrics, and data sources.
Just drawing one extra architecture diagram with a few more lines that looks a bit more complex.
Just memorizing a few extra algorithm names that sound impressive but never get used.
optionExplanations: 讲得快不是层级差异,内容深度和取舍才是。
对;L5 的增量正是取舍+fan-out 论证+指标体系+数据源,比 L4 的单目标更完整。
架构图复杂度不等于范围深度,取舍论证才是。
多背名词是知识堆砌,不是 L5 要求的取舍能力。
optionExplanations_en: Speaking faster is not the level difference; content depth and trade-offs are.
Correct — L5's increment is trade-offs plus a justified fan-out plus a metric system plus data sources, more complete than L4's single objective.
Diagram complexity is not scope depth; trade-off reasoning is.
Memorizing terms is knowledge stacking, not the trade-off ability L5 requires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量排序模型区分正负样本能力的离线指标,越接近 1 越好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) is an offline metric of how well a ranker separates positives from negatives, closer to 1 is better.

scenario: feed 排序题很容易被广告排序、通知、搜索这些相邻子系统带偏,时间不够用。
scenario_en: A feed-ranking question easily drifts into ad ranking, notifications, and search, and you run out of time.
q: 开场为什么要显式声明范围外(广告排序/通知/搜索)?
q_en: Why explicitly declare out-of-scope (ad ranking/notifications/search) in the opening?
why: 显式声明「除非被要求,先不做广告排序、通知、搜索」是防止范围蔓延:把有限时间聚焦在核心 feed 排序上,而不是被相邻子系统拖散。这是主动的范围管理,不是回避。
why_en: Explicitly saying 'unless asked, exclude ad ranking, notifications, search' prevents scope creep, focusing limited time on core feed ranking rather than adjacent subsystems.
tradeoff: 显式声明范围外(聚焦核心·控时间) vs 不声明(被相邻子系统拖散·答不完)
options: 只是为了显得自己什么子系统都懂,借此炫耀一下知识面
因为这些相邻子系统在技术上根本没法实现,必须被排除掉
防止范围蔓延,把有限时间聚焦核心排序,不被相邻子系统拖散
因为面试官事先明确下令禁止提到广告排序这件事
options_en: Just to look like you know every adjacent subsystem, showing off breadth for its own sake.
Because these adjacent subsystems are technically impossible to build at all, so they must be excluded.
To prevent scope creep and focus limited time on core ranking, not get dragged into adjacent subsystems.
Because the interviewer explicitly ordered beforehand that ad ranking must never be mentioned.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官明确说「就想听你怎么把广告插进 feed」,那广告排序就进范围,不该再排除。
optionExplanations: 声明范围外是为聚焦不是炫耀;罗列子系统反而分散注意力。
这些子系统技术上完全可做,排除是时间取舍不是不可行。
对;主动声明范围外是控时间的范围管理,把火力集中在核心问题。
面试官没禁止;是你主动划范围以聚焦,必要时可被要求纳入。
optionExplanations_en: Declaring out-of-scope is for focus, not showing off; listing subsystems scatters attention.
These subsystems are entirely feasible; excluding them is a time trade-off, not infeasibility.
Correct — proactively declaring out-of-scope is time-managing scope control, concentrating fire on the core.
The interviewer does not forbid it; you scope proactively to focus, and it can be pulled in if requested.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开场主动排除相邻子系统(广告/通知/搜索),聚焦核心问题、控时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An out-of-scope declaration proactively excludes adjacent subsystems (ads/notifications/search) to focus on the core and manage time.

scenario: 把三个业务目标映射到可训练的 ML 代理目标。
scenario_en: Map the three business objectives to trainable ML proxy objectives.
q: 下列「业务目标 → ML 代理」的映射,哪些是对的?(多选)
q_en: Which 'business objective → ML proxy' mappings are correct? (multiple)
why: 参与度→P(click)/E[dwell];有意义连接→P(meaningful interaction);创作者公平→重排里的曝光公平约束。三者代理不同、可测性不同,不能用同一个信号糊弄。
why_en: Engagement→P(click)/E[dwell]; meaningful connections→P(meaningful interaction); creator equity→an exposure-fairness constraint in re-ranking—distinct proxies with distinct measurability.
options: 参与度 → P(click) / E[dwell time]
有意义连接 → P(meaningful interaction)
创作者公平 → 重排里的曝光公平约束
创作者公平 → 最大化 P(click)
options_en: Engagement → P(click) / E[dwell time].
Meaningful connections → P(meaningful interaction).
Creator equity → an exposure-fairness constraint in re-ranking.
Creator equity → maximize P(click).
optionExplanations: 对;点击/停留是参与度最直接的可测代理。
对;有意义互动概率专门刻画回复/私信/评论串这类深度连接。
对;创作者公平不是打分头而是重排里的约束,分配曝光份额。
错;最大化点击恰恰会向头部集中、伤害创作者公平,方向相反。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — clicks/dwell are engagement's most direct measurable proxy.
Correct — meaningful-interaction probability specifically captures deep connections like replies/DMs/threads.
Correct — creator equity is not a scoring head but a re-ranking constraint allocating impression share.
Wrong — maximizing clicks concentrates at the top and harms creator equity, the opposite direction.

termDefinitions.term: exposure-fairness constraint / 曝光公平约束
termDefinitions.meaning: 在重排阶段按目录占比等标准分配曝光份额,兑现创作者公平。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An exposure-fairness constraint allocates impression share by criteria like catalog share in re-ranking, realizing creator equity.
